newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ASTLE STEERS NZ TO 228 VS ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ASTLE STEERS NZ TO 228 VS ENGLAND.

text.p: A dashing 94 by Nathan Astle helped New Zealand post a competitive 228 for eight from their 50 overs in the fifth and final one-day cricket international against England at the Basin Reserve on Tuesday.
Astle got New Zealand away to a flyer, but some good bowling by the English after a wayward start soon brought the innings back to a level pegging.

After Bryan Young was out in the 7th over, caught by keeper Jack Russell off paceman Andrew Caddick for 11, Stephen Fleming and Astle looked comfortable in progressing New Zealand's score to 80 after 17 overs.

But just when the two looked to be building a solid partnership, Fleming was out lbw to spinner Robert Croft, and new batsman Chris Cairns fell shortly thereafter, caught behind off Craig White for one. Adam Parore quickly followed them back to the hut, out lbw to Caddick after hitting 18.
But Astle kept New Zealand in the game. He was in fine touch, sweeping, driving and hooking with consumate ease.
Astle was dismissed just six runs shy of his fourth one- day century when he chipped Caddick to mid-on, only to watch England skipper Mike Atherton take a brilliant catch, low and to his left.
Astle's 94 came off 129 balls in 184 minutes and included 10 fours.
At his demise, the New Zealand innings crumbled.

Captain Lee Germon was unlucky to be given out lbw to a Chris Silverwood ball which hit him high on his pad above the leg roll. But Harris then skied a Darren Gough delivery for an easy catch at long-off, and bad running saw Gavin Larsen run out for a duck.

Dipak Patel and Heath Davis saw New Zealand safely through to the close of the innings and ensured the home side had a reasonable total to defend. But 229 to win is by no means an impossible task for England on a good batting wicket.

Caddick was the best of the English bowlers, taking three for 35 off his 10 overs, while fast medium Chris Silverwood struggled for line and length, his 10 overs costing 53 runs for just the one wicket.
Silverwood's eight wides also boosted extras to a handy total of 26 for New Zealand.
England led 2-1 going into this game, with the third match at Napier ending in a tie, and New Zealand must win here to draw the five-match series.
